angleRead.name: Jordan Velez
angleRead.text: I'm standing at the counter of the corner spot near the Baylight District, coffee going cold, thinking about Marine Systems. They shed two workers this cycle and growth is negative — a three-person shop down to one person, Mina Linas, who's out there monitoring sea level rise while the rest of the team disappears. That's the story. Not the AI researchers at Anthropic with their $649.8M in revenue and security guard at the door. Not the construction authority adding headcount. The contraction. The science outfit that's supposed to be tracking the water eating the edges of this city, and it's down to one technician. Mina Linas is the one I want to talk to. I want to stand where she works, ask

plan.focus: Marine Systems shedding half its staff in a booming district — what the contraction means for the work and for the block
plan.why: The ledger shows Marine Systems at 3 employees, down from 5, with negative growth, in a district where the big employers are all up. One of the named workers is the sea level monitoring technician — the person whose job is literally about the city's exposure. If the monitoring is getting thinner while the construction and AI money gets thicker, that's a story about what the boom is and isn't paying for.
checks: Talk to Mina Linas first — she's the one who survived the cuts, she knows what the work is now
Ask what the monitoring actually covers — is she covering the same waterfront with fewer hands?
Reach Philly Rodriguez at Oakland Casino Town — the house is steady but down a body, and the roster lists organized crime as a role, which raises questions about what kind of business the casino is
Check with Keisha Ramos at the redevelopment authority — the district is being rebuilt around these businesses, what does the authority know about Marine Systems' trajectory?
Walk the block between Anthropic and Marine Systems and gauge the difference in foot traffic, security presence, and general momentum
